yaml_example:
# flows/overdue-reminders.yaml - every morning, tell each owner which invoices are overdue
on:
  schedule:
    cron: "0 9 * * *"

jobs:
  remind:
    steps:
      - id: due
        run: sql
        with:
          query: "SELECT id, user_id, number FROM invoices WHERE status = 'sent' AND due_on < date('now')"
      - for_each: ${{ steps.due.outputs.rows }}
        as: inv
        steps:
          - run: notify
            with:
              user_id: ${{ inv.user_id }}               # the recipient's _benmore_users.id
              title: "Invoice ${{ inv.number }} is overdue"
              body: "Open it to send a reminder."      # optional
              link: "/invoices/${{ inv.id }}"           # optional
              type: warning                             # optional: info | success | warning | error
client: bm.notifications.onNew((n) => toast(n.title));  // fires for the recipient only, also for cron-created notifications
behavior: `user_id` (required) is the recipient's user id (`_benmore_users.id`); after interpolation it must be a whole number greater than 0, and it is bound as a SQL parameter. One recipient per step: put the step in a `for_each:` to notify several users.

`title` (required, not empty), `body` and `link` (optional) are text; `type` is info, success, warning or error (default info; a literal anything else is refused when written, a `${{ }}` value that renders anything else is stored as info). Each `${{ }}` resolves once: a request value lands in the title or body as text and is never resolved again. A link with a script-capable scheme (javascript:, data:text/html) is dropped and the notification kept, as for a hook.

It is stored and announced exactly like a hooks.yaml `notify:`: it appears in GET /api/_notifications, counts in /api/_notifications/count and `{{notification_count}}`, and its live `{table:'_benmore_notifications', action:'insert'}` event reaches only the recipient's own SSE/WebSocket streams - never the caller, other users or admins - whatever started the flow (request, cron, async job, data event). So bm.notifications.onNew fires for it.

A recipient id that names no user fails the step and stores nothing, so an account created later with that id never inherits it. The flow's answer gives the fixed reason `the notification could not be created` (the step error, for an app admin, says `no user has id N`). Catch it with an `on_error:` handler on the step when a missing recipient is expected. A recipient that is not a whole number fails the same way.

In a `transaction: true` flow (or a scheduled flow with `on.schedule.transaction: true`) the notification is written in the transaction and announced after COMMIT; a rollback keeps and announces nothing. Without a transaction it is durable, and announced, when the step returns, even if a later step fails. An on_error handler runs outside the transaction.

The flow is the authorization: the step notifies whichever user id it is given, in any tenant. When the id or the text comes from request input, check first that the caller may notify that user (a `run: sql` with `expect_rows` against a membership or ownership row) and rate-limit the route.
Outputs: `steps.<id>.outputs.id` (the notification id) and `.user_id`. Approved MCP commands and read-only connector flows refuse the step.
